newsitem.title: UK: UK spot natgas centres on weekend, mostly softer.
newsitem.headline: UK spot natgas centres on weekend, mostly softer.

text.p: The UK spot natural gas market saw a spate of trades for weekend gas, with large volumes moving, traders and brokers said.

A single lot of 230,000 therms a day was traded at 9.30 pence a therm, but most trade was done at higher prices, with several deals totalling at least 250,000 therms a day reported at 9.60 pence a therm.
It was also widely rumoured that more deals were done at 9.70 pence a therm, although this was not confirmed.
"The weekend's been very volatile," said a trader, "although the majority (of trade) has been done in the mid nines."
The interest in the weekend took some players by surprise, especially as demand is not expected to be particularly high.
"It's been a while since there's been any interest in the weekend," said one.

Transco announced a demand forecast of 204 mcm for Saturday, the same as for Friday, and representing 48 percent of peak day demand. This is despite lower temperatures, with Transco forecasting 7.9 Celsius for Saturday, down from a seasonal normal 9.2 Celsius.
Further out, most prices were softer where changed, with the fourth and first quarters and the October gas year all losing ground.

There was some interest seen for trading individual months, as opposed to whole quarters. This is a change from recent weeks which have seen trade in individual months largely displaced by trade in quarters, especially since the launch of the IPE contract.

One dealer said that there was no particular significance to the change, and he pointed out that the May/June strip done on Friday had to be done that way as the second quarter, in which both months fall, is already under way.

At the NBP, the third quarter traded at least twice at 10.30 pence, but there was not the same interest at St Fergus. One seller said he had offered 10.20 pence for the quarter, but the bids never came above 10.10 pence and no deals were concluded.

There was also interest further forward, with deals reported in the fourth, first and second quarters. Q2 98 trade at 11.10 pence surprised a broker who said he thought a deal had also been done at 10.90 pence.

The IPE futures contract saw a disappointing day's trade. Only 85 lots were traded in four separate deals, with only a single 25-lot deal done in the two-hour afternoon session. All months with the exception of June and July closed softer, echoing the sentiment on the physical market.
